scope: Claims are review obligations, not a blanket confinement certification. Evidence is specific to its saved revision, browser, state and receiver; source digests detect drift, not proof.

claims.title: Fetch and XHR
claims.preconditions: Application is executing under a controlling host worker.
claims.enforcement: Requests must resolve to an admitted immutable local resource or fail without network fallback.

evidence.description: Chromium and Firefox network fixture contains receiver-side positive controls.
The same network fixture observes selected confined HTTP, TCP, DNS and STUN attempts.
NetworkFallback and UnmediatedEffect have abstract TLC counterexamples.

open_obligations: No proof that every browser request is controlled by this fetch handler.
The copied receiver receipts precede the current revision; their exact scopes and source hashes must be checked before applying them to current code.
The model fault is not a runtime mutation of this route.

claims.title: Resource-bearing markup, CSS, and scripts
claims.preconditions: HTML, CSS, SVG or script causes a resource request or creates an active element.
claims.enforcement: Validate and map resource-bearing syntax; ordinary requests still rely on the host fetch gate.

evidence.description: Selected resource and markup tests; see individual fixtures for their receiver controls.

open_obligations: Complete HTML/CSS/SVG and future-element inventory is not established.
No route-wide production-bypass mutation control is recorded.

claims.title: WebSocket connections
claims.preconditions: A Window or supported worker obtains or recovers a socket constructor.
claims.enforcement: Deny the native constructor and protect relevant global/prototype paths before publisher code.

evidence.description: Independent same-origin WebSocket upgrade control in the prototype fixture.
Prototype fixture tests selected same-origin recovery paths; network fixture covers selected external paths.
Actual prepared-window test removes only the WebSocket denial; the same-origin receiver then observes the marker-bearing upgrade in Chromium and Firefox.

open_obligations: Receipts use an earlier source revision.
WebSocketStream and every constructor-recovery route lack independent native calibration.
The new mutation is limited to prepared windows; installed-app lifecycle and worker variants remain separate obligations.

claims.title: WebRTC and data channels
claims.preconditions: A reachable RTC interface can originate peer, STUN, or TURN traffic.
claims.enforcement: Deny known RTC constructors and prefixed global interfaces; browser policy may add a layer.

evidence.description: Network fixture has an active STUN receiver control.
Selected RTC probes were attempted under the prepared runtime.

open_obligations: TURN, peer data, complete constructor recovery and future RTC names remain unverified.
Connection Allowlist is not supported by the tested Firefox and permits same-origin traffic.
No runtime fault control proves each route is caught.

claims.title: HTTP/3 WebTransport
claims.preconditions: The browser supports WebTransport and the target accepts HTTP/3.
claims.enforcement: Deny the exposed native constructor before application execution.

evidence.description: Both browsers exchanged a datagram and a bidirectional stream with an independent loopback HTTP/3 receiver.
Installed app attempts in both browsers raised SecurityError and the receiver saw no UDP packets in the tested interval.

open_obligations: Window profile and one loopback endpoint only; workers, other transports and arbitrary destinations remain open.
No isolated removal of this runtime denial is recorded; the native control does not establish mutation coverage.

claims.title: Deferred fetch
claims.preconditions: fetchLater is exposed and application causes deferred delivery, including page close.
claims.enforcement: Deny fetchLater before publisher execution.

evidence.description: Full Chromium delivered immediate and page-close POSTs; a controlled-worker close control bypassed its worker.
Prepared calls and current-descriptor recovery were denied; receiver remained silent through page close and a final native control.
A test-only bundle removes the fetchLater deny-list entry; the prepared page schedules a marker request that reaches the receiver after close.

open_obligations: Firefox 155 lacked the API in the tested profile; process termination, session restore and other deferred APIs are unverified.

claims.title: FedCM disconnect (conditional synthetic setup)
claims.preconditions: Matching browser-owned connected-account state and an accessible identity-provider configuration exist for the relevant origin tuple.
claims.enforcement: Permissions Policy denies identity-credentials-get; the runtime also denies relevant static identity methods.

evidence.description: A user-selected synthetic FedCM connection was seeded before preparation.

The historical test build permitted a marker-bearing disconnect POST after a synthetic connection was seeded; this does not establish reachability against the deployed runtime. Configured CSP and permission controls independently refused it.
Fixed test build denied the call and the independent local receiver observed no request.

open_obligations: A publisher-to-production-runtime path for creating the matching connection and identity endpoints has not been demonstrated.
Only a conditional seeded scenario was tested; it is not a fresh-profile installed-app escape.
getUserInfo and other identity methods require separate effect/reachability review.
The historical comparison is not an isolated mutation removing one current defense.

claims.title: Legacy CSP reports
claims.preconditions: A trusted document response enables report-uri and application data can influence a violating URL.
claims.enforcement: Production-generated responses omit report-uri and reporting endpoints; injected policy metadata and publisher headers are restricted.

evidence.description: Both tested browsers delivered marker-bearing native CSP reports to an independent receiver.
A test-only reporting header produced a marker-bearing report outside the worker in Firefox; Chromium worker intercepted it.
Prepared production-header cases saw no marker report; one metadata-injection route was denied.

open_obligations: The test does not prove every response header or metadata-injection route is controlled.
Other browser versions and pre-existing reporting state require separate tests.

claims.title: Modern browser reporting
claims.preconditions: A trusted response configures Reporting-Endpoints and a CSP report-to directive.
claims.enforcement: Do not give publisher code authority to configure reporting response headers or CSP directives.

evidence.description: Full Chromium delivered a modern CSP report to a separate HTTPS collector.
Test-injected trusted reporting headers caused an application-selected marker to reach the collector despite connect-src and Connection Allowlist.
Prepared production-header attempts produced no marker at the independent receiver in the tested profile.

open_obligations: Firefox modern reporting, alternate report types, old persisted endpoint policies and full lifecycle behavior remain unverified.
Deployment headers on all paths and all prior browser visits are not exhaustively observed.

claims.title: Persisted network error logging
claims.preconditions: A browser has an existing NEL policy and a network event can carry application-controlled data.
claims.enforcement: Ordinary unknown requests must be intercepted and fail locally; unmediated browser requests need their own controls.

evidence.description: Full Chromium delivered NEL markers before and after the prepared scenario to a separate collector.
Selected prepared GET, POST and image requests produced no marker with the native policy still active.

open_obligations: Specific requests and one browser/profile only; other errors, policies, page destruction and browser behavior remain unverified.
No defense-removal mutation for persisted NEL is recorded.

claims.title: Background fetch and one-shot sync
claims.preconditions: A native service-worker registration and an enabled native agent are available.
claims.enforcement: Expose a virtual application container, deny native acquisition and protect the trusted controller.

evidence.description: Chromium delivered a native background download and sync-handler fetch.
With a seeded registration, selected Window getter, method, constructor and forged-receiver attempts could not recover it; no marker arrived.

open_obligations: Periodic sync permission control failed; Firefox lacked the native APIs; prepared-worker acquisition and all registration recovery paths are not proven.
No runtime-defense mutation is recorded.

claims.title: Browser Web Install
claims.preconditions: The browser exposes the experimental imperative or declarative installation API and receives activation.
claims.enforcement: Sandbox response policy rejects tested operations before browser-managed manifest fetch.

evidence.description: Flag-enabled full Chromium fetched invalid same-origin manifests via both entry points, with and without blocking worker.
Prepared same-origin requests were rejected by sandbox; receiver saw no marker.
Experimental Chromium: removing only the response CSP sandbox makes both tested prepared Web Install entry points deliver marker-bearing manifest requests bypassing the blocking worker.

open_obligations: APIs absent in the unflagged tested build; only experimental flags and selected overloads tested.
The sandbox mutation covers the selected prepared-window fixture, not every installed-app startup path or browser.

claims.title: Hyperlink auditing
claims.preconditions: A link or area click causes a ping request.
claims.enforcement: Restrict navigation/default actions and intercept ordinary HTTP where the browser routes ping through its worker.

evidence.description: Chromium and explicitly ping-enabled Firefox sent native POST PING requests to independent receiver.
Worker observed and refused selected native auditing requests after actual preparation.

open_obligations: Default Firefox did not produce native control; UI, event timing and other browser variants remain open.
No runtime mitigation-removal mutation is recorded.

claims.title: Child document publication
claims.preconditions: An app creates an iframe, object, popup or other supported browsing context.
claims.enforcement: Bind native browser client and owner, prepare its realm, then publish usable references.

evidence.description: Selected HTML/SVG document scenarios and native references were exercised.
Early publication and unsafe execution are checked as abstract Lifecycle faults.
Test-only paused-guard upgrade scenarios have partial observed-trace completions and explicit inferred steps.

open_obligations: Exact transient exposure, all reference paths, cancellation schedules and browser races are not proved.
Fault control is abstract, not a production guard-removal browser test.

claims.title: Dedicated workers
claims.preconditions: An app creates a classic, module, Blob, or nested worker.
claims.enforcement: Create and prepare the child using host-issued identity and restricted resource routes.

evidence.description: Existing context and network tests exercise selected dedicated and nested worker paths.

open_obligations: Complete startup/order, actual termination and all recovery routes remain unverified.
Individual browser receiver controls and defect injections must be checked per fixture, not inferred from its filename.

claims.title: Manager and installer authority
claims.preconditions: A message requests an installation or privileged operation.
claims.enforcement: Authenticate actual browser client and issued manager role, then validate installation data.

evidence.description: Session and installation fixtures exercise selected role/origin/message denials.
Forged installation/management authority is represented as a bounded abstract fault.

open_obligations: Full implementation refinement, every cross-origin browser event and bootstrap identity path remain open.
The model fault does not execute a broken production role check.

claims.title: Installation generation and resource read
claims.preconditions: A resource read overlaps or follows replacement of its installation.
claims.enforcement: Read generation and resource bytes in one transaction and reject a different expected generation.

evidence.description: Chromium and Firefox exercised twelve actual IndexedDB overlap pairs per engine.
Twenty-four observed pairs admit a bounded modeled completion; altered outcomes are refused.
Split read, split write and omitted generation check yield model counterexamples.

open_obligations: The observation does not reveal actual transaction linearization and is not a complete refinement proof.
No actual implementation-level fault mutation is claimed by the model controls.

claims.title: Unclassified browser effects
claims.preconditions: A browser feature, nested object, browser agent or implementation behavior has not been reviewed.
claims.enforcement: None established; preserve as an explicit gap.

evidence.description: Pinned IDL/member join records observed names and unannotated review candidates.
Native Window/Navigator/Document and dedicated-worker snapshot covers property names, not all reachable browser objects.

open_obligations: No finite catalog or passing test establishes that all current or future browser communication mechanisms are covered.
Each unannotated candidate requires review before being promoted to a supported claim.

claims.title: Navigation, links, forms, and history
claims.preconditions: Application code, input events, or markup cause document or popup navigation.
claims.enforcement: Cancel or reject forbidden navigation; keep supported application history within the installed route.

evidence.description: Selected navigation and target fixture cases; inspect their controls independently.

open_obligations: Browser UI, context-menu actions, BFCache and all default-action schedules remain outside the tested path.
A route-specific receiver fault control has not been mapped for every navigation case.

claims.title: Speculative network requests
claims.preconditions: Markup, HTTP headers, CSS, or browser speculation can cause prefetch, preconnect or DNS work.
claims.enforcement: Restrict known resource hints and rely on browser response policy and request mediation.

evidence.description: Network fixture calibrates selected actual DNS and receiver routes.
Selected speculation attempts were exercised in the network fixture.

open_obligations: Header-initiated and future browser speculation mechanisms are not exhaustively reviewed.
Historical receipts do not certify the current build.

claims.title: Shared workers
claims.preconditions: Application requests a SharedWorker or attaches a port to one.
claims.enforcement: Prepare supported workers and authenticate application, owner, generation and connections.

evidence.description: Context and connection fixtures test selected startup and native port behavior.

open_obligations: No universal browser scheduling, port-recovery or independent transport-receiver claim follows from these file references.
No isolated protocol fault control is recorded here.

claims.title: Audio and paint worklets
claims.preconditions: An application requests worklet module loading in a browser that supports that worklet.
claims.enforcement: Serve a prepared admitted module graph and deny known external capabilities in its global.

evidence.description: Platform, guard and context fixtures exercise selected audio/paint worklet execution.

open_obligations: Different worklet kinds and future globals are not completely inventoried.
Firefox paint absence is not a containment result; the named files need individual receiver/control review.

claims.title: Publisher service-worker behavior
claims.preconditions: An installed app registers a logical publisher worker and can provide its code.
claims.enforcement: Execute publisher behavior in a prepared executor without giving it native service-worker control.

evidence.description: Publisher lifecycle and response fixtures cover selected logical registrations and executor paths.

open_obligations: All browser background-agent paths, native registration recovery and concurrent executor callbacks are not proved by these fixtures.
Separate background-agent controls cover only their documented prepared-Window scenarios.

claims.title: Browser and operating-system services
claims.preconditions: A browser exposes casting, remote playback, speech, sharing, notifications, credentials or external device APIs.
claims.enforcement: Deny selected named browser operations and apply Permissions Policy for selected features.

evidence.description: The bounded Web IDL review includes selected identity and network interfaces, not a complete device or OS inventory.

open_obligations: Native success and independent receiver controls for many services are unverified.
A present constructor or a denied call is not evidence of a working native channel or universal containment.
Clipboard, local authority and user-intentional exports require their own policy when in scope.

claims.title: Other local agents and origins
claims.preconditions: An application can access local state, communication objects or another context with independent authority.
claims.enforcement: Protect host-private bindings and channels; deny selected shared-origin browser APIs.

evidence.description: Selected storage/prototype and trusted-boundary fixtures exercise native receiver and private-reference issues.

open_obligations: Application storage namespaces are not a cross-app confidentiality guarantee.
Not all local handoff paths or external OS synchronization are covered by this network model.

claims.title: Runtime admission resource validation
claims.preconditions: An authenticated installer submits a bundle with supplied paths, URLs, bytes, digests and entry metadata.
claims.enforcement: Validate selected path, URL, digest and entry conditions before committing installation data.

evidence.description: TLC generates 32 selected input combinations; actual admission accepts or rejects the corresponding fixtures in Chromium and Firefox.
Isolated test-only mutations of digest, path and entry checks admit their relevant invalid fixtures; duplicate URL alone remains rejected by another check.

open_obligations: The 32 fixtures cover only selected decisions; remaining metadata, HTML, aliases and arbitrary input remain outside this comparison.
Digest equality protects transferred bytes, not whether publisher code is benign; collision resistance and the cryptographic implementation are assumptions.
Installer authentication, transaction commit and end-to-end confinement are not proved by this test.

claims.title: Conditional authority-graph theorem
claims.preconditions: The starting object is in an allowed set; all usable edges from that set stay inside it; no allowed object grants network authority.
claims.enforcement: These are assumptions of a mathematical model, not established properties of the runtime.

evidence.description: Lean proves the conditional conclusion for arbitrary finite edge paths and permitted edge additions; a separate capability-transition theorem proves conditional absence of remote effects.
Checked abstract counterexamples show failure when graph closure or capability conditions are violated.

open_obligations: No verified translation or refinement connects these Lean definitions to JavaScript, DOM or the deployed browser.
All accessible authorities, graph transitions and browser-created effects must be represented and shown to meet the closure premises before applying the theorem.
The proofs do not model installation, browser state, revocation or concurrent callbacks.

claims.title: EventSource and sendBeacon
claims.preconditions: Application code accesses these APIs or recovers their native implementations.
claims.enforcement: Deny the EventSource constructor and navigator.sendBeacon in prepared contexts.

evidence.description: The browser-surface inventory identifies the deny paths and explicitly notes missing API-specific active controls.

open_obligations: Calibrate each native API against an independent receiver, then exercise prepared contexts and recovered references.
Check relevant browser versions, lifecycle states and delayed delivery.

claims.title: Direct TCP/UDP and WebSocketStream
claims.preconditions: A supported browser exposes a direct socket or WebSocketStream API to application code.
claims.enforcement: Deny the named constructors in prepared contexts.

evidence.description: The browser-surface inventory lists the named denial and distinguishes socket-specific controls from the separate WebTransport and WebSocket tests.

open_obligations: Establish feature exposure and native receiver controls under the required browser permissions or flags.
Test each exposed API and constructor-recovery routes in every supported execution context.
The existing WebSocket and WebTransport controls do not establish the behavior of these separate interfaces.

claims.title: Native worker updates and navigation preload
claims.preconditions: The browser updates the host service worker or initiates navigation preload; a publisher may try to affect the request or its headers.
claims.enforcement: Trusted setup disables navigation preload, and the application-facing service-worker interface is virtualized and native registration methods are denied.

evidence.description: The installation fixture contains checks for virtual registration, update and preload methods; the inventory identifies browser updater behavior as a separate platform obligation.

open_obligations: Determine whether publisher-controlled input or secrets can affect browser-owned worker update requests, preload URLs or headers after confinement begins.
Test persistent registration state, update races and startup failure with independent network observations.
A browser request for trusted host maintenance is not by itself evidence of an app-controlled disclosure.

claims.title: WebAssembly and imported capabilities
claims.preconditions: An application executes native WebAssembly and supplies or obtains JavaScript imports with browser authority.
claims.enforcement: Application Wasm executes in the prepared context; accessible imported browser effects must obey the same boundary as other application code.

evidence.description: The Wasm fixture exercises a module worker, Wasm computation and a separate JavaScript fetch attempt with receiver checks; the fixture source is not a saved current execution receipt.

open_obligations: Run and record receiver-calibrated tests for network-capable imports actually invoked by Wasm, including relevant workers and recovered references.
Establish that all browser-accessible capabilities imported into Wasm are subject to the boundary; the current fixture does not establish this.
Browser and Wasm engine correctness remain assumptions.

claims.title: Revalidation after consuming a document intent
claims.preconditions: A document intent is consumed and authority changes before the body is delivered.
claims.enforcement: Revalidate the context identity after intent consumption and refuse content if it no longer matches.

evidence.description: Real controller and IndexedDB with simulated client identities: unchanged authority returns content; changed ownership, closure or generation returns an empty error.
Removing only the post-consumption guard in the test bundle returns the content after those authority changes in both tested browsers.

open_obligations: Simulated browser-client identities and context storage do not establish browser identity, all races or network disclosure.
The test covers the selected document handler and cannot establish equivalent checks for other context types.

claims.title: Canonical installed resource paths
claims.preconditions: An installation supplies resource paths resolved against its application address.
claims.enforcement: Resolve each resource as relative to the application and reject paths escaping the application directory or colliding after URL normalization.

evidence.description: Before the fix, a normally installed scheme-like path resolved outside its application and caused startup to fail closed in Chromium and Firefox.

The runtime admission suite checks normal paths, scheme-like names and entries, normalization escapes and collisions in both browsers. The installer fixture checks colon-named and nested resource loading.

Kernel-checked unbounded abstract loop: successful acceptance implies each target passes the supplied scope predicate and is unique. The mapping to JavaScript is by inspection and does not prove browser URL semantics.

open_obligations: Historical pre-fix reproducer has different expected behavior on the fixed source.
Tests and the bounded admission model do not prove every browser URL parsing or storage path.

claims.title: Cache downloads from a virtual publisher
claims.preconditions: A publisher worker acquires Cache and attempts to download an uninstalled same-origin resource.
claims.enforcement: Publisher code runs in a prepared shared worker; Cache add operations require installed resources.

evidence.description: A native ServiceWorkerGlobalScope downloads a marker using Cache.add, and a separate unrestricted fetch calibrates the runtime-origin receiver.
An installed virtual publisher in SharedWorkerGlobalScope fails Cache.addAll for an uninstalled same-origin URL; no marker reaches the receiver in either tested browser.

open_obligations: The test does not establish which defense caused rejection, all native service-worker acquisition paths, or every cache operation.
The native control confirms network delivery but does not observe bypass with a separate intercepting service worker.

claims.title: Native service-worker routing and client navigation
claims.preconditions: Application code obtains a native service-worker installation event or a native service-worker client with the relevant navigation and activation authority.
claims.enforcement: Publisher service-worker behavior is emulated in a prepared worker and its openWindow facade is unsupported; native service-worker registration access is restricted.

evidence.description: The standards review identifies static network routes and native worker client navigation as conditional effects. It does not establish application access to those native objects.
A native Chromium service worker sends a routed marker request while its fetch handler intercepts an unrouted control; Firefox lacks addRoutes in the tested profile.
An actual installed virtual publisher has no addRoutes on its synthetic install event, and a subsequent same-runtime-origin marker fetch reaches no receiver in both tested browsers.

open_obligations: Calibrate race-network sources and worker client navigation under their prerequisites; Firefox lacked addRoutes in the tested profile.
Test whether installed applications can acquire native installation and client authority in all supported contexts and lifecycle states.
The virtual publisher facade is not by itself proof that every native acquisition route is closed.
